install_tell: pip install agno  (pip install 'agno[os]' for server mode; AgentOS served via agent_os.serve() on localhost:7777 by default; AGENT_OS_PORT overrides)
misconfig_patterns: AgentOS deployed with no OS_SECURITY_KEY and no JWT config -> all /agents, /teams, /workflows, /config, /schedules endpoints fully open (auth OFF by default per agno/os/auth.py)
Default CORS whitelist includes app.agno.com -- any agno.com subpath can reach a local dev instance if port 7777 is exposed
DOCS_ENABLED defaults true -- GET /openapi.json exposes full API surface unauthenticated; GET /docs renders interactive Swagger on open instances
authorization=True flag required on AgentOS() to enforce JWT RBAC -- default is False even when JWT middleware is wired
Telemetry calls to os-api.agno.com are separate from local auth; agent metadata flows to Agno cloud by default

active_probe.false_positive_check: The /health {"status":"ok","instantiated_at":"<ISO8601>"} pair is distinctive -- the instantiated_at field is Agno-specific. Corroborate with GET / returning {"name":"AgentOS API","id":"...","version":"1.0.0"} for high confidence. GET /info is unauthenticated and returns agno_version + agent/team/workflow counts -- a vendor-unique response schema. Do NOT rely on http.title:"Agent UI" alone -- it is generic SPA branding (Agent UI is the separate hosted frontend at app.agno.com, not served by AgentOS itself). http.html:"agno-agents" is the canonical Shodan dork (Python package name appearing in bundled JS when Agent UI frontend is self-hosted); verify with /health instantiated_at before classifying. NOTE: Complete brand transition from Phidata to Agno as of early 2025 -- all Phidata/phidatahq dorks return zero. ssl:"agno.com" hits vendor infra only, not third-party deployments.

deployment_tells: Port 7777 open with FastAPI JSON at / returning {"name":"AgentOS API","id":"...","version":"1.0.0"} (default port, AGENT_OS_HOST=localhost by default -- internet exposure requires explicit 0.0.0.0 bind or proxy)
GET /info returns agno_version + agent/team/workflow/model counts unauthenticated
GET /openapi.json exposes full API schema (DOCS_ENABLED=true by default)
SvelteKit Agent UI frontend at localhost:3000 connecting to AgentOS backend on 7777
Swagger docs at /docs titled 'Agno AgentOS' on default deploys
WebSocket /workflows/ws endpoint active with authenticate/start-workflow action protocol
pivot_paths: GET /info -> agno_version + registered agent/team/workflow counts (unauthenticated, high value for scoping)
GET /openapi.json -> full API schema enumeration including all route paths and schemas (unauthenticated default)
GET /agents -> enumerate all registered agent IDs and display names
GET /config -> full OS config including all registered agents/teams/models (requires auth on hardened deploy, open on default)
GET /models -> LLM provider inventory (reveals which cloud APIs are wired)
GET /agents/{agent_id}/runs -> agent execution history and session content
GET /schedules -> reveal scheduled agent jobs and their configurations
auth_evidence: libs/agno/agno/os/auth.py: get_authentication_dependency() returns a passthrough (allows all requests) when OS_SECURITY_KEY is unset AND JWT is not configured. AgentOS constructor default is authorization=False. JWT middleware requires explicit opt-in via authorization=True on AgentOS() or manual middleware setup. OS_SECURITY_KEY bearer token is the simpler path but must be set by operator -- not provisioned by default. Default AGENT_OS_HOST=localhost provides implicit protection on same-machine deploys; however cookbook examples and Docker deploys commonly bind 0.0.0.0. Result: any internet-exposed AgentOS with default env vars = fully open REST API + WebSocket. Agno cloud Agent UI (app.agno.com) is in the CORS whitelist by default.
sensitive_assets: Registered agent definitions via GET /agents (system prompts, tool wiring, model provider selection)
Full OS configuration via GET /config (agent definitions, model API keys potentially embedded in config objects)
Agent/team/workflow run history and session content via run listing endpoints
LLM provider inventory via GET /models (reveals which cloud APIs are in use)
Scheduled job definitions and execution history via /schedules
Memory and knowledge base contents via /memory and /knowledge
Real-time agent execution via POST /agents/{id}/runs on unauthenticated default deploy (SSE streaming execution without auth)
